newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shipyard workers occupy government building.
newsitem.headline: Polish shipyard workers occupy government building.

text.p: About 300 workers of the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, birthplace of Poland's Solidarity union, began an occupation of the local governor's building on Monday to demand state help to save their jobs.
The workers launched an indefinite protest after inconclusive talks with the governor on credit guarantees.
"We are staying here until we see results. Either we will be restructured or murdered," Jerzy Borowczak, the head of the shipyard's Solidarity union, told reporters.
The governor of northern Gdansk province, Henryk Wojciechowski, wrote a letter to the treasury minister after meeting the protesters, saying the state-controlled firm's 5,000 staff was getting angry.
"The lack of a clear perspective about the future, be it liquidation or restructuring, is causing an uproar," Wojciechowski wrote.

Karol Guzikiewicz, a yard Solidarity official, suggested that unless the government prepared a plan to save the company, workers might stage protests similar to those in 1970, when marches against food price rises led to bloody clashes with the police and the military.
The shipyard -- where Lech Walesa's Solidarity union was born 16 years ago in the fight against communism -- went bankrupt in June owing more than 300 million zlotys ($110 million).
The receiver says borrowing of $150 million would allow it to continue five of 17 outstanding contracts, and perhaps survive until a buyer is found.
The government says it is looking for a strategic investor but refuses to guarantee new loans as banks insist.
"The possibilities of burdening taxpayers with costs of Gdansk shipyard restructuring have been exhausted," Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said last Friday.
The government, dominated by an ex-communist party since 1993, says the shipyard was driven to bankruptcy by unprofitable contracts signed by previous management.
But critics accuse the the government, which has subsidised other collapsing companies, of refusing to bail out the shipyard because of spite towards an opposition stronghold.
The shipyard now has debts of 415 million zlotys ($148 million), including 127 million zlotys owed to the treasury. About 2,000 workers have been laid off or found other jobs.
